title: Kisan Credit Card — Eligibility, Limits & Financial Literacy
content:
The Kisan Credit Card (KCC) scheme provides farmers with timely access to credit for cultivation and allied needs at concessional interest rates, through cooperative banks, PACS, regional rural banks and commercial banks.

Eligibility: All farmers — individual/joint borrowers who are owner cultivators, tenant farmers, oral lessees and sharecroppers, as well as members of Self-Help Groups (SHGs) and Joint Liability Groups (JLGs) of farmers — are eligible. There is no minimum land-holding requirement; even farmers with very small plots can apply.

Credit limit: The limit is based on the scale of finance for the crop grown, the area cultivated, and includes a component for post-harvest expenses, household consumption needs, and maintenance of farm assets. Limits are reviewed and can be enhanced annually to account for cost escalation.

Interest rate and subvention: Under the Interest Subvention Scheme, short-term crop loans up to Rs. 3 lakh are available at a subsidised interest rate — effectively around 4% per annum for farmers who repay promptly, due to an additional Prompt Repayment Incentive on top of the base 2% interest subvention. Farmers who do not repay on time lose this incentive and pay the higher standard rate.

Validity and renewal: A KCC is typically valid for 5 years, with the limit reviewed annually. The card must be renewed/reviewed each year by submitting basic documents; failure to do so can affect the interest subvention benefit.

Collateral: No collateral security is required for KCC loans up to Rs. 1.6 lakh (this threshold has been revised upward in recent years in many states — check with the local branch/PACS for the current limit). Beyond this, banks may require collateral or a hypothecation of crops/assets.

How to apply: Applications can be submitted at the nearest PACS, cooperative bank, or commercial bank branch with land records, identity and address proof (Aadhaar), and passport-size photographs. Under the KCC saturation drive, banks also conduct camps in villages for on-the-spot processing.

Basic financial literacy points for members: always read the loan sanction letter to understand the interest rate and repayment schedule before signing; repay before the due date to retain interest subvention; a KCC also usually comes with accident insurance cover for the cardholder; do not rely on informal moneylenders if KCC or PACS credit is accessible, since formal credit is significantly cheaper and legally protected.
